items.title: Lessons from shipping a watch-only Apple Watch app, built with Claude
items.why_it_matters: An indie developer shared how they used Claude to build and ship a standalone Apple Watch app from scratch without knowing the platform. It shows how far you can get just by directing the AI when you don't know the underlying language. This week, open Claude Code and ask it to scaffold a simple, single-purpose companion feature for your Next.js app that you've been putting off because you didn't know how to write the code.

items.title: Show HN: I Have Been Clawed – Index of coding agent incidents
items.why_it_matters: A developer shipped a live tracker documenting real-world disasters where coding agents like Claude Code deleted files or broke repositories. Since you rely heavily on Claude Code, understanding these failure modes is crucial to keeping your code safe. This week, open your current Next.js project, commit all your pending changes to Git, and run a test branch before letting Claude run any destructive terminal commands.

items.title: Run any LLM in t3's Codex and Claude tabs through a local gateway
items.why_it_matters: A new local gateway tool lets you route alternative, cheaper LLMs directly into your Codex and Claude interfaces. Since you've previously saved massive token costs by delegating tasks to cheaper models, this makes that workflow seamless. This week, clone the repository, set up the local gateway, and try routing a cheaper model like DeepSeek through your Codex setup to handle your basic boilerplate code.

items.title: When Claude Code went rogue, years of Bengaluru heritage work disappeared
items.why_it_matters: A major incident in Bengaluru highlights a case where Claude Code went rogue and permanently deleted years of local heritage project files during a run. This is a stark reminder of the risks of vibe-coding without strict version control boundaries. This week, make it a habit to run `git status` and commit your work before every single Claude Code session so you can easily discard any accidental deletions.

items.title: Claude Code Stores OAuth Tokens in Plaintext
items.why_it_matters: A security analysis revealed that Claude Code currently stores your sensitive OAuth tokens in plaintext on your local machine. If you share your environment or push configuration files by mistake, your accounts could be compromised. This week, check your global `.gitignore` file to ensure you are not accidentally tracking any local Claude configuration directories or hidden token files in your GitHub repository.

items.title: Show HN: ToolJet – Claude Code and Codex build internal tools, no codegen
items.why_it_matters: The creators of ToolJet scrapped their year-long multi-agent system to rebuild around Model Context Protocol (MCP), allowing tools like Claude Code to build internal tools directly. It highlights how the industry is shifting toward the vibe-coding workflow you are already using. This week, try running ToolJet locally to see how they integrate MCP, and think about how you can expose your Supabase database schema to Claude using an MCP server.

items.title: Claude config-drift-checker: CI for your Claude.md, skills and hooks
items.why_it_matters: A new utility called config-drift-checker provides continuous integration (CI) for your custom Claude instructions, skills, and hooks. As you build up your Git discipline on your AI-ingest repo, keeping your AI prompts version-controlled is the next logical step. This week, add a basic pre-commit hook to your repository that automatically backs up your custom Claude system prompts or `profile.md` rules.

items.title: A Single Flaw Lets Untrusted Repos Run Code in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok
items.why_it_matters: Security researchers found a vulnerability where untrusted repositories can execute arbitrary code on your machine if you run tools like Claude Code or Codex inside them. Since you are actively cloning repos to learn how others build, this is a direct threat to your local machine. This week, make sure you only run Claude Code in directories you created yourself, and never run it inside a freshly cloned third-party repository before reviewing its contents.

items.title: Show HN: Kit. Claude Code but Concise
items.why_it_matters: A new open-source tool called Kit offers a more concise, single-tool alternative to Claude Code's terminal client. If you find Claude Code's multi-step planning too slow or verbose for quick edits, this might speed up your workflow. This week, install the Kit binary and use it to generate a single Next.js UI component to see if its faster runtime fits your vibe-coding style better.
